name: hospitality-python
what_it_holds: Municipal (Chapel Hill, NC) internal repo with two scripts: extract-airbnb-properties.py (uses the unofficial nderkach/airbnb-python API client) and extract-vrbo-properties.py (basic screen-scraping of Vrbo listing pages), aggregating output into a single CSV of short-term rental listings with lat/long for the town. Marked 'internal use only - experimental'; authors note data quality is low and manual cleanup is required.
why_useful: One of very few public repos that actually attempts a Vrbo listing pull (gap #9, competitor/adjacent supply). Method only, not usable as-is (low quality, unofficial API, would need running against live sites which is a ToS question), but demonstrates the closest thing to a Vrbo scraper with a real, if small, municipal use case (Chapel Hill).
time_coverage: unknown / one-off pull, no dated vintages
size_hint: small municipal CSV, unspecified row count

name: booking-sites-parser
what_it_holds: Apache-2.0 Python CLI parser (28 commits, 3 stars) for Booking.com, Homeaway.com and Airbnb.com listing pages; installable as `booking-sites-parser` package, run via `python -m booking_sites_parser <url>`. No data fields documented in README beyond usage examples; no data files committed; has a /tests directory.
why_useful: A generic multi-site (incl. Homeaway) listing parser could in principle be pointed at Vrbo/Expedia vacation-rental pages to pull price/amenity fields, addressing gap #9, but it is unmaintained tooling with no data attached and unclear scope; scraping would also be a ToS decision.
themes: Vrbo / HomeAway datasets and scrapers, Vrbo listing snapshots, Expedia Group vacation rental supply data
why_all: A generic multi-site (incl. Homeaway) listing parser could in principle be pointed at Vrbo/Expedia vacation-rental pages to pull price/amenity fields, addressing gap #9, but it is unmaintained tooling with no data attached and unclear scope; scraping would also be a ToS decision.

One tool covering three relevant platforms (Homeaway + Booking.com + Airbnb) in one schema, which would ease cross-platform supply comparisons under gap #9 if it still works against current site markup (unclear given age/inactivity).
